profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Teacher Higher Education Profile
authoring_note: This file rewrites progression in practitioner-friendly language using original wording. It is intended for feedback and coaching, not for reproducing source-framework text.

entries.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Teacher Higher Education Profile
entries.friendly_description: Getting the basics done. In this role, the person can keep important digital activity moving, but progress still depends too much on familiar routines, examples or nearby help.
entries.strengths_message: This is a workable starting point for teacher he practice because core activity can continue, especially when examples and support are available.
entries.development_message: The next step is to make choices more deliberate and repeatable so that capability does not depend on a single familiar routine.
watchouts: Owning or accessing many apps means the basics are secure.
Getting through the task once shows the process is reliable.
coaching_questions: Which recurring tasks still break down when the context changes?
What one shared routine would make your digital work easier to recover and follow?
entries.feedback_snippet: You can already keep important digital activity moving in this area. Focus next on creating one dependable routine that works even when conditions change.

entries.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Teacher Higher Education Profile
entries.friendly_description: Running dependable digital workflows. In this role, digital choices are usually intentional and dependable, with enough independence to handle common variation and minor problems.
entries.strengths_message: This level shows dependable day-to-day practice and sound judgment in familiar and moderately complex situations.
entries.development_message: The next step is to move beyond strong personal practice and start shaping reusable, evaluative or group-level improvement.
watchouts: Being quick personally is the same as having a good workflow.
A preferred tool is automatically the right choice everywhere.
coaching_questions: Where do your current workflows create hidden friction for other people?
How do you decide when a new tool is actually worth adopting?
entries.feedback_snippet: You are using digital practice with intent and reasonable independence in this area. The strongest next move is to make that practice easier for other people to benefit from.

entries.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Teacher Higher Education Profile
entries.plain_language_label: Improving digital workflows for wider benefit
entries.friendly_description: Improving digital workflows for wider benefit. In this role, digital capability extends beyond strong personal practice into reusable improvement, guidance or influence for wider groups.
entries.strengths_message: This level shows influence as well as skill: practice is not only strong personally but also improves outcomes for others or for the wider context.
entries.development_message: The next step is to sustain influence without over-complexity, keeping practice evidence-led, inclusive and adaptable.
watchouts: Proficiency means always adopting the newest or most advanced platform.
If a process works for experts it should work for everyone.
coaching_questions: What evidence shows that your workflow improvement really helped others?
Which parts of the process should be simplified rather than expanded?
entries.feedback_snippet: You show mature digital practice here, including judgment and influence. Keep checking that innovation remains proportionate, well-evidenced and inclusive.
